sections.title: Stochastic simulation
sections.text:
At the steady state, the scarcest species is complex_A at 162.7 molecules in 1e-18 L (concentrations read as mM; one mM is 602.2 molecule(s)). For a birth-death process the stationary distribution is Poisson, so the standard deviation is sqrt(N) and the relative fluctuation is 1/sqrt(N) = 7.8% here. That is below the ~20% the model's constants are uncertain by, so the fluctuation is no longer the biggest error in the deterministic answer. That is a much weaker claim than the ODE being right: the noise is still there, and it is only smaller than the uncertainty you already have. This is a statement about the MEAN at steady state. Rare events -- a switch flipping, a transcript that never appears -- have probabilities that fall exponentially with the copy number and never reach zero, and nothing here bounds them.

Horizon 6.24695 s -- 4 x the slowest settling time (1.56), derived from the Jacobian's smallest non-zero eigenvalue.

918 event(s) to t=6.247 of a requested 6.247, from seed 11: reached the end of the requested window. Final counts: complex_A=156, complex_AB=446, complex_B=156 in 1e-18 L. One realisation. It is not a mean and not a prediction -- another seed gives a different trajectory of the same process, and any quantitative claim needs an ensemble whose seeds are stated.

Counts were taken from concentrations in mM at 1e-18 L. Both were stated rather than assumed: the network IR records neither, and each changes every count here by whatever factor the guess was wrong by.
